answer: In an ember detection market, each paid alert includes a certified sensor signature over its reading and a fresh beacon nonce. The registry assigns one hourly reward quota to each physical sensor; all agent accounts presenting its signatures share that quota, and replayed alerts earn nothing. An echo of the same reading through 1,000 aliases cannot produce 1,000 payments. Scaling requires buying and deploying more certified sensors. Enrollment must reject cloned keys and test sensor locations; hardware scarcity raises attack costs without proving every reading accurate.
